question.worked_solution:
Since $p$ varies directly with $q,$ we use the equation

$$
p=kq.
$$

We are told that $p=-35$ when $q=-7.$ We substitute this data into the equation to find $k:$

$$
\begin{aligned}-35 & =k\cdot (-7) \\ \frac{(-35)}{(-7)} & =k \\ \frac{35}{7} & =k \\ 5 & =k\end{aligned}
$$

So, the direct variation equation is given by

$$
p=5q.
$$

Finally, substituting the value of $q=-6$ into this equation gives

$$
\begin{aligned}p & =5\cdot (-6)=-30.\end{aligned}
$$
